title: 1tqhx6b
Differences in worship and belief
hook: The same Qur'an, the same Prophet: what reading does the Ja'fari practice in the call to prayer, the prayer and the prostration rest on?
scenes.0.text: Azan is the call to prayer recited by **Bilal** from a high place during the time of the Prophet. According to some accounts, at that time, the ezan sometimes included the phrase "Hayye ala hayri'l-amel", which means "To the best of deeds". The validity of these rumours is disputed, and the practice is reported to have been abandoned afterwards. Some accounts say that this phrase was removed from the Quran by Caliph Umar. The Jaffa school maintained this expression as an essential part of the torture. Today, in the Shia prayer, after the call to prayer and victory, this phrase is also recited and invites the believers to the best deed.
scenes.0.art.actors.0.label: 39sy1h
Bilal
scenes.1.text: In the case of Ja'far, "Hayye ala hayri'l-amal" is considered a virtue of the persecutor. According to tradition, Caliph Umar abolished this phrase so that people would prefer prayer to jihad and weaken the spirit of war. The Shi'a hadith reads "Ashhedu enne Aliyyen waliyyullah", which means "I bear witness that Ali is Allah's protector". It reads like a decent slogan. On the other hand, the phrase "Es-salatu hayrun mine'n-nevm", which means "Prayer is better than sleep", does not appear in the Ghafir al-azan. In Sunni sources, this phrase is mentioned as a fixed circumcision in the morning prayer.
scenes.1.art.actors.0.label: 1h556w8
Muezzin
scenes.2.text: The position of the hands in prayer also varies from sect to sect. In most Sunni denominations, the person praying is bound to his or her chest or belly while standing, and this is considered circumcision. In the Maliki sect, it is said to be a view to fold the hands sideways. The hands are left on the sides, and the hands are tied. The Shiites continue this practice of prostration as the prayer of the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt. That's why a Shiite and a Sunni praying side by side in a mosque have their hands separated.
scenes.2.art.actors.0.label: q33sx7
Worshipper
scenes.2.art.actors.1.label: q33sx7
Worshipper
scenes.3.text: The algebra b. In a narration from 'Abdullah, the Prophet said: "The earth has become a mosque for me and my Ummah and a means of my worshipping". The Jafari jurisprudence, based on this hadith, stipulates that prostration should be made to the ground or to something that comes from the ground, which cannot be eaten or worn. Things like carpet or fabric don't meet that requirement. That's why many Shiites carry around a small piece of earth called a "seal" and place their forehead on it during prayer. The soil of Karbala is particularly preferred for this stone. In Sunni sects, the place of worship is wider. The carpet, hay or soil can be kneeled on.
scenes.3.art.actors.0.label: 1br6cqq
In prostration
scenes.4.text: The love for the land of Karbala comes from the fact that it is the place where Husayn was martyred. Some legends associate this land with healing and reward, but the validity of these legends is also disputed among Shia scholars. In Shi'ite sects, prostration to the ground is obligatory, while the use of a seal made of the soil of Karbala is considered proper. The use of seals is not forbidden in Sunni sects. The seal for the Jafari school is a continuation of the Prophet's prostration to the ground. And the choice of the land of Karbala is a reminder of the blood that has been shed on that land.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.5.text: According to Ibn Abbas, the Prophet combined noon and evening, evening and evening in Medina without fear, rain or travel. When asked why, Ibn Abbas replied that he did not want to impose hardship on the Prophet's Ummah. On the basis of this hadith, Jafari jurisprudence permits the unjustified combination of prayers, i.e. the jam. According to him, the time between noon and noon is the same as the time between noon and evening, and the time between sunset and midnight is the same as the time between evening and evening. But the prayers at different times are more virtuous. In Sunni sects, the same hadith is often explained with a special excuse. The Hanafis do not accept the jumu'ah except when they are on a journey or during the fast.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.6.text: One night of Ramadan, Caliph Umar entered the mosque and saw people performing night prayers in scattered groups. They 've been sent to Ubey b. He gathered the people from behind the House and said, "This is a good bid'ah". In Sunni sects, terawih is sunnah and this collection is considered legitimate with the acceptance of the sahabah. In Ja'far fikih, the Nafilah prayer of the nights of Ramadan is performed individually. The terawih performed by the congregation is not considered the Sunnah of the Prophet, but the practice of Caliph Umar. The word "bid'at" that came out of Umar's own mouth is also especially remembered in this reading.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1wnvat7
Umar
scenes.7.text: In Surah Anfal, verse 41, it says that one-fifth of what you take as spoils belongs to Allah, the Prophet, the near of kin, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer. The Jafari jurisprudence broadens the meaning of the word "spoil" in the verse and gives one-fifth, or hummus, of the increase in one's annual earnings. The humus splits into two equal parts. The first is the imam's share. The second is for the seyyid, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer. During the absence, the imam's share is spent under the supervision of the mujttahid. In Sunni sects, the verse is only valid for war booty and no humus is taken from the booty. Indeed, the people of the House are among the nearest.
scenes.7.art.actors.0.label: 16pen9g
Merchant
scenes.7.art.actors.1.label: xbhgan
Mujtahid
scenes.8.text: Some days and hadiths also have different meanings in the two schools. The Hadith of Ghadir, in which the Prophet said, "Ali is the guardian of the one I am the guardian of", is also found in Sunni books. But it is debated whether the word "mevlâ" means ruler or friend. Ashura Day is a fast day in Sunni sources and commemorates the deliverance of Moses from Pharaoh. On this day, the martyrdom of Husayn is also remembered. However, the Amish dynasty gave this day different meanings to forget the persecution of the Prophet's grandson on the day of Ashura. He spread stories linking the drowning of Pharaoh and the landing of Noah's Ark to this day. He invented many superstitions based on no solid source, such as that the house of the one who leaves the dishes open at the table on this day will be blessed. The aim was to cover up the memory of the bloodshed at Karbala, and unfortunately they succeeded in doing so to a great extent. Today, the vast majority of Muslims think of Ashura as a dessert, but unfortunately not Karbala. In the Cafiir tradition, the first ten days of Muharram and Ashura are days of mourning for Karbala. The 18th of Zilhicce is also celebrated as the feast of Ghadir, because on that day the Prophet Ali raised his hand.
scenes.8.art.actors.0.label: 3qh9mj
Imam Husayn
scenes.8.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
scenes.9.text: Allah only desires to remove the filth from you, O people of the House, and to purify you. According to the hadith of Kisâ in Muslim, the Prophet took **Ali**, **Fatimah**, **Hasan** and Husayn under his cloak and recited this verse. Buhari in 6585, the Prophet announces that some of his friends will be taken away from him at the pool on the day of judgment. The Qur'anic reading considers the Tathir as proof of the innocence of the Ahl al-Bayt. And He judges the Companions by their conduct and their knowledge. In Sunni sources, the Ahl al-Bayt are loved, but innocence is the property of the prophets. The pool hadith is also associated with apostates or hypocrites. In the Qur'an, the verse is addressed to the five people who are under the ummah.
scenes.9.art.actors.0.label: 19izoul
The Prophet
scenes.9.art.actors.1.label: lhg99z
Imam Ali
sunni.0.says: Caliph Umar gathers people behind Ubayy b. Ka'b on a Ramadan night and says, "What a good innovation (bid'a) this is"; he also says that the prayer performed in the last part of the night is more virtuous.
sunni.1.says: The Prophet says that some of his companions will be driven away at the Pool; the answer is given, "You do not know what they innovated after you."
sunni.2.says: From Jabir: "The earth has been made for me and my community a place of prostration and a means of purification (tayammum)." In Sunni sources it is cited as evidence that earth is a place of prostration.
sunni.3.says: Ibn Abbas says that the Prophet combined the noon and afternoon, and the sunset and night prayers, in Medina without fear or rain, and that the reason was not to put his community in hardship.
sunni.4.says: The Prophet takes Imam Ali, Fatima, Imam Hasan and Imam Husayn under his cloak and recites the verse Ahzâb 33:33.
sunni.5.says: Differences in the narrative of Ezan's words; the narrative that Ibn 'Umar said "hayye billa hayri'l-amal" is known from secondary sources, its validity is debatable.
sunni.6.says: The relaying of the Maliki school's opinion on letting the hands hang down in prayer (sadl); the report of Caliph Umar concerning the Ramadan night prayer (qiyam).
sunni.7.says: The Ghadir hadith is also found in Sunni hadith books.
shia.0.says: Reports from the imams on the adhan, khums and taqiyya, and the meaning of Ghadir.
shia.1.says: The reports on which Shia jurisprudence rests concerning the place of "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" in the adhan, letting the hands hang down, combining prayers and the place of prostration.
shia.2.says: Reports on making prostration on what grows from the ground, prostration on the earth of Karbala, and the distribution of khums.
shia.3.says: A summary of the Shia view and the scholars' details.
disputes.0.title: 1bgyqqm
The phrases of the adhan
disputes.0.shia: The phrase "Hayya ala khayr al-amal" is mentioned in some early reports. In Ja'fari jurisprudence it is a part of the adhan; the testimony to Imam Ali is not a condition but a recommended emblem. "As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm" is not recited in the Ja'fari adhan.
disputes.0.sunni: The phrase "Hayye ala hayr'l-amel" is mentioned in some early narratives. This is not read in the Sunni Azan; "es-salatu hayrun mine'n-nevm" is the Sunnah of the morning azan. There are also stories about Ibn 'Umar.
disputes.1.title: efgmld
The position of the arms
disputes.1.shia: The position of the hand in prayer is discussed in both jurisprudences. In Ja'fari practice the hands hang down; folding them is regarded as invalidating the prayer.
disputes.1.sunni: The position of the hand in prayer is discussed in both jurisprudences. In the majority the hands are folded; in the Maliki school the opinion of letting them hang down has also been relayed.
disputes.2.title: 1oiv1xc
Seal and place of worship
disputes.2.shia: Prostration on earth has evidence in both traditions. In Ja'fari jurisprudence prostration is made on what grows from the ground; earth from Karbala is recommended.
disputes.2.sunni: Prostration on earth has evidence in both traditions. In the Sunni schools the place of prostration is free; al-Bukhari 335 reports that the earth was made a place of prostration.
disputes.3.title: 8x097a
Combining prayers
disputes.3.shia: The hadith that the Prophet combined prayers in Medina is mentioned in both sources. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, combining without excuse is permissible; praying separately is more virtuous.
disputes.3.sunni: The hadith that the Prophet combined prayers in Medina is mentioned in both sources. The Sunni schools mostly tie this combining to an excuse (Muslim, Sahih).
disputes.4.title: fs4ose
Tarawih
disputes.4.shia: That Caliph Umar gathered the congregation on a Ramadan night also appears in al-Bukhari 2010. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, tarawih in congregation is not sunna; the supererogatory prayer is performed individually.
disputes.4.sunni: That Caliph Umar gathered the congregation on a Ramadan night also appears in al-Bukhari 2010. In the Sunni schools tarawih is sunna and is regarded as legitimate with the acceptance of the Companions.
disputes.5.title: 67piz1
Khums
disputes.5.shia: The one-fifth ruling of Anfal 8:41 is accepted in both schools. In Ja'fari jurisprudence khums is paid on annual earnings; there are the Imam's share and the sayyids' share.
disputes.5.sunni: The one-fifth ruling of Anfal 8:41 is accepted in both schools. In the Sunni schools the verse is specific to war spoils; no khums is taken from earnings.
disputes.6.title: 1x2xti7
Taqiyya
disputes.6.shia: The dispensation to speak under duress is mentioned in both sources, with the Ammar incident and the related verses. In Ja'fari jurisprudence, taqiyya is permissible in danger to life, property and honor, and sometimes obligatory.
disputes.6.sunni: The dispensation to speak under duress is mentioned in both sources, with the Ammar incident and the related verses. In Sunni jurisprudence, taqiyya is a dispensation at the moment of coercion; it is not regarded as a constant principle.
disputes.7.title: 1r97kd0
Ashura and Ghadir
disputes.7.shia: The day of Ashura and the Ghadir hadith are known in both traditions. In the Ja'fari calendar, Ashura is mourning and 18 Dhu al-Hijja is the festival of Ghadir.
disputes.7.sunni: The day of Ashura and the Ghadir hadith are known in both traditions. In Sunni practice Ashura is a fast day; the word "mawla" is interpreted as friendship.
disputes.8.title: 1jkwlfn
Infallibility and the justice of the Companions
disputes.8.shia: The verse of purification and the Kisa hadith mention the Ahl al-Bayt in both sources. In Ja'fari belief the Ahl al-Bayt are infallible (ma'sum) through this verse; the justice of the Companions depends on a measure.
disputes.8.sunni: The verse of purification and the Kisa hadith mention the Ahl al-Bayt in both sources. In Sunni belief all the Companions are just; infallibility is specific to the prophets. The hadith of the Pool is attributed to apostates or hypocrites.
questions.0: If in Muslim the Prophet's combining is explained as "not to put his community in hardship," how does this reason help in understanding the prayer times?
questions.1: If the hadith that the earth was made a place of prostration is in both sources, does the difference in the place of prostration stand between the condition of earth and freedom?
questions.2: How does Caliph Umar's calling tarawih a "good innovation" bring his own word to the fore in whether an act of worship is regarded as sunna or not?
questions.3: How does Ammar b. Yasir's word under duress show the limit of taqiyya with respect to life and faith?
questions.4: How do the hadith of the Pool (al-Bukhari 6585), love for the Companions and the measuring of conduct stand side by side?
summary: Differences such as the adhan, the position of the hands, the place of prostration, combining, tarawih, khums and taqiyya arise from two readings of the same verses and hadiths. The Ja'fari school explains them as a continuation of the Qur'an and the Prophet's practice. The Sunni schools too draw their own practices from the same texts.
key: Differences in the adhan, prayer and prostration
notes.0: In the adhan, «Hayya ala khayr al-amal» is recited in Shia jurisprudence, «as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm» is not.
notes.1: In prayer the hands are left hanging in Shia jurisprudence, and folded in most Sunni schools.
notes.2: In Shia jurisprudence prostration is made on earth or on something that grows from the ground; in the Sunni schools it is free.
notes.3: The practices of combining prayers, tarawih and khums are different.
notes.4: Ashura is for commemorating the suffering of Karbala; Ghadir, however, is the joy of Imam Ali's wilayat.
